newsitem.title: UK: U.S. companies to buy Yorkshire Electricity. [CORRECTED 15:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: U.S. companies to buy Yorkshire Electricity. [CORRECTED 15:00 GMT]

text.p: Yorkshire Electricity Group Plc said Monday it had agreed to be acquired for 1.5 billion pounds ($2.4 billion) in cash by a company owned by American Electric Power Co. Inc. and Public Service Co. of Colorado.

Yorkshire, which was one of Britain's last two remaining independent regional electricity companies, said the bid equalled 927 pence ($15.03) a share, which represents a premium of 13.3 percent to its closing price of 818.5 pence ($13.27) Friday.
(Corrects conversion of share figures into dollars from $5.73 and $5.06).

Yorkshire, which is based in Leeds, England, said the bid by the newly formed Yorkshire Holdings was 11.3 times Yorkshire's earnings per share, before exceptional items, for the year ended March 31, 1996.
The current Yorkshire Electricity management team will continue in their roles after the deal, the American companies said.
No other details were immeidtaely available.

American Electric Power, which is based in Columbus, Ohio, provides electricity to industrial, commercial and residential customers in Ohio, Indiana, Michigan, Virginia, West Virginia, Kentucky and Tennesse.
Public Service of Colorado, based in Denver, provides electricity, gas and steam in Colorado and parts of Wyoming.

"We can both add to Yorkshire Electricity's aspirations in the UK. We can also learn valuable skills and, together, look at other opportunities in the UK and further afield," the two U.S. companies said in a statement.
They said Yorkshire Electricity shareholders would retain the right to receive the interim dividend of 15.80 pence (25.6 cents) per share net.
